doc.title: Joe Wilder Part 2 interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 12, 1998

title: Rough start for black Marines in the South
summary: Integration of the Marines was hard, with only white officers in authority and Southern racial conditions made harsher by the military.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Was there a period of adjustment or any unpleasantness in the fact that the Marines had just become integrated?

Yeah, it was rough in the beginning. It was a pretty rough situation because there were no black officers and there were only a few black non-commissioned officers, corporals and maybe a couple of buck sergeants. But that came later actually. So that all the personnel with any authority were white, all the personnel. And of course we were in the middle of the south, so conditions were based on the racial problems that we had prior to that, and of course in the military it was a lot more severe. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -3-
